title: Chana chaat
skill: A tangy dressing tasted and fixed

notes.text: Mix the dressing in a bigger bowl, and taste it on a few chickpeas before it all goes in.

move.title: Sour, salty, a little spicy
move.body: Chaat is a family of tangy snacks sold at street stalls all over India. Chana chaat is the chickpea one: chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, and green onion in a lime dressing with chaat masala, a salty, sour spice mix. This is the unit's mastery week, so you'll make it on your own and fix the dressing by taste.

why.title: A spice mix that's sour
why.body: Chaat masala is made with dried green mango powder, black salt, and cumin. It tastes sour and salty at once, which is why chaat is so tangy. Ground cumin and an extra squeeze of lime come close if you can't find it.

why.title: Fix one thing at a time
why.body: Taste on a few chickpeas. Too sour, add a little honey. Flat, a pinch of salt. Not tangy enough, more lime. Change one thing, taste again, and you'll know which change helped.

why.title: Seeds out, salad crisp
why.body: The watery middles of cucumbers and tomatoes thin the dressing. Scooped out, the salad stays crisp and the dressing stays strong.

why.title: Rinse the chickpeas
why.body: The liquid in the can is salty and thick. Rinsed chickpeas take the dressing better and let you decide how salty the salad is.

why.title: A few minutes to soak in
why.body: Chickpeas are firm, so the dressing needs a few minutes to soak in. Unlike a lettuce salad, this one gets better as it sits.

wrong.fix: Stir in a little honey, ¼ teaspoon at a time, and taste again.
Add more chickpeas or cucumber. Next time, leave out the chili flakes.
Add a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lime, stir, and taste again.

wrong.sign: There's a puddle in the bowl
wrong.fix: The seeds were left in. Spoon the salad out with a slotted spoon, or pour off the liquid.

quiz.q: What makes chaat masala taste sour?
quiz.explain: It's sour and salty at once.

quiz.q: The salad is too sour. What do you add?

choices: The can's liquid is salty and thick
quiz.explain: Then you decide how salty it is.

quiz.q: Why can this salad sit before you eat it?
choices: Firm chickpeas get better as they soak

ingredients.prep: or ½ tsp ground cumin and an extra squeeze of lime

steps.text: Read the recipe through. Set out every tool and ingredient before you start.
steps.tip: This is your mastery week. You make it on your own.

steps.text: Open the chickpeas and drain them in the colander.
steps.tip: Keep your fingers away from the lid's cut edge.

steps.text: Rinse the chickpeas under cold water and shake them dry. Tip them into the large bowl.
Lay a damp paper towel under the cutting board. Rinse the cucumber, tomatoes, green onions, and cilantro.
steps.look: Push the board gently. It shouldn't slide.

steps.text: Peel the cucumber in long strokes, away from you.
steps.tip: Hold it by the top end, on the board.

steps.text: Trim the ends and cut it in half the long way. Scrape out the seeds with a spoon.
steps.look: A clean groove down each half.

steps.text: Cut each half into thin sticks, then across into small pieces about the size of a chickpea. Add them to the bowl.
steps.look: Pieces the same size as the chickpeas.

steps.text: Halve the tomatoes through the stem. Cut out the cores and scoop out the seeds.
steps.tip: Point the knife tip away from your hand.

steps.text: Cut the tomato halves into strips, then across into small pieces. Add them to the bowl.
steps.look: Pieces about the size of a chickpea.

steps.text: Trim the green onion roots. Slice the onions into thin rings and add them to the bowl.
steps.tip: Set the knife down flat, blade away from you, when you're done.

steps.text: Pull the cilantro leaves off the stems and tear them into the bowl.
In the small bowl, whisk the lime juice, olive oil, chaat masala, cumin, honey, and salt. Add the chili flakes if you like heat.
steps.look: The spices all mixed in, no dry clumps.

steps.text: Pour the dressing over the salad and stir. Taste a spoonful with a few chickpeas.
steps.tip: Too sour: honey. Flat: salt. Not tangy: lime.

steps.text: Fix one thing, stir, and taste again. Write down what you added.
Let it sit, then stir and serve. Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
